faculty_decisions.text: Accept the overall GI pressure causal architecture for DEVELOPMENT. Do NOT recalibrate untreated deterioration, early blood/volume response or delayed rescue merely to resemble legacy.

FR-G requires targeted recalibration. The target is NOT an exact pressure curve. The target behavior is: slow 1-L crystalloid infusion over 60 min during active hemorrhage -> modest, transient attenuation of deterioration, NOT near-stabilization. The resulting trajectory should remain meaningfully closer to the untreated course than to a rapidly/responsively resuscitated course. No exact mmHg target is supplied.
Do NOT fit FR-G directly. Any correction must operate through the GENERAL crystalloid volume/retention mechanism. No case-specific multiplier. No FR-G-specific branch.
Preserve previously closed volume behavioral constraints (R30, R60, R120, Rpeak and the closed volume behavioral calibration region). Do not violate those constraints to satisfy FR-G.

Source control remains absent from the current GI management mechanism. Do NOT invent source-control physiology in this package. Instead: verify and document whether continued bleeding remains active during FR-B and other treated scenarios; identify whether early improvement eventually reverses if bleeding continues. This is analysis first.

Norepinephrine is now a HIGH-PRIORITY FUTURE MANAGEMENT MECHANISM. Desired future architecture: norepinephrine -> common vascular tone T -> pressure / perfusion -> downstream delivery/debt, with volume/pump interaction. Do NOT implement it in this package. Add/update technical debt / roadmap only.

scenarios.faculty_comment_verbatim: The common-core direction is correct, but the magnitude of deterioration is too small. I would expect the trajectory to remain closer to the untreated course, with only modest transient attenuation from the crystalloid.
scenarios.faculty_conclusion: Direction is correct, but the magnitude of deterioration is TOO SMALL. One litre normal saline infused over 60 minutes during ongoing hemorrhage appears to provide excessive sustained hemodynamic protection.
faculty_mechanistic_concern: a slow infusion should not behave like an effective rapid volume challenge;
the trajectory should remain substantially closer to untreated deterioration, with only modest transient attenuation.
scenarios.title: 72f slow crystalloid infusion
